title: Process change followed by an escape at end of line
engineering_question: A manufacturing process change was implemented and defects subsequently escaped detection. What went wrong in both the process and the detection system?
one_liner: Investigate this manufacturing quality escape and determine corrective action.
initial_input: Two components were rejected at final assembly leak test, both traced to the same supplier production week, following a process change at that supplier.
expected_impacted_domains: Supplier process control and change management
Battery thermal performance consequences of degraded braze coverage
High voltage safety exposure from coolant ingress
expected_reasoning_paths: There are two distinct problems - an occurrence problem, TR-032 process, and a detection problem, TR-033 measurement capability - and the 8D must address both
RC-003 identifies that the dew point alarm threshold was set above the qualified limit after the process change, which is a change management failure rather than an operator error
TR-032 also found coverage below minimum, which links to FM-007 and therefore to the thermal capability investigated in SCN-003
TR-034 passes on post-containment samples but does not clear the originally affected population, so containment scope must be defined by production week, not by sample result
known_unknowns: RC-003 is not confirmed - the furnace atmosphere record for the affected week is not in the environment
The number of plates from the affected week already built into vehicles is not represented
No thermal measurement exists on packs containing affected plates
data_classification: SIMULATED ENTERPRISE ARTEFACT - not OEM, customer or proprietary data
